testCases.input: My name is Anjali and I am studying the LLM evals course. What is the difference between model evals and application evals?
testCases.actualOutput:
Hello Anjali! It's great that you're diving into the LLM evaluations course. The distinction between model evaluations (model evals) and application evaluations (application evals) is quite important, so let’s break it down.

Model evaluations are focused on assessing the language models themselves. This means you're looking at how well the LLM performs in various tasks and benchmarks. Essentially, it's about evaluating the capabilities and limitations of the model in isolation.

On the other hand, application evaluations are concerned with LLM-based applications. This involves assessing how well these applications utilize the language model to perform specific tasks or provide services. Here, the focus is on the effectiveness of the application as a whole, rather than just the underlying model.

To summarize, model evals judge the performance of the LLM itself, while application evals evaluate how well an application that uses the LLM functions. Understanding this distinction is crucial as it helps you navigate the evaluations you'll be doing in your work as an AI engineer.
